statement:
The assertions in this section concern **abelian presheaves**, not abelian sheaves; the functor and exactness claims must not be transferred to sheaf categories. $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\prod_{(i_0,\dots,i_p)}\mathcal F(U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_U U_{i_p})$ with the alternating restriction differential, and $\check H^p$ denotes its cohomology. The $\delta$-functor structure is induced by short exact sequences of abelian presheaves and their associated cochain complexes.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms
with fixed target such that all fibre products
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p}$ exist in $\mathcal{C}$.
The functors $\mathcal{F} \mapsto \check{H}^n(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})$
form a $\delta$-functor from the abelian category $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal{C})$
to the category of $\mathbf{Z}$-modules (see
Homology, Definition \ref{homology-definition-cohomological-delta-functor}).
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a category, $\mathcal U$ a family of maps to one object admitting all required iterated fibre products.
conclusions: For $n\ge0$, the functors $\mathcal F\mapsto\check H^n(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ form a cohomological $\delta$-functor $\mathrm{PAb}(\mathcal C)\to\mathrm{Ab}$.

\label{lemma-cech-cohomology-delta-functor-presheaves}

Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ a family of maps with fixed target and all finite iterated fibre products over $U$, and consider abelian presheaves on $\mathcal C$. The chain complex $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal U,\bullet}$ is the degreewise direct sum of free represented abelian presheaves with alternating face-map differential, as constructed at sites-cohomology.tex:970–1003.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let
$\mathcal{U} = \{f_i : U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms
with fixed target such that all fibre products
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p}$ exist in $\mathcal{C}$.
The chain complex $\mathbf{Z}_{\mathcal{U}, \bullet}$ of presheaves
of Lemma \ref{lemma-cech-map-into} above is exact in positive
degrees, i.e., the homology presheaves
$H_i(\mathbf{Z}_{\mathcal{U}, \bullet})$ are zero for $i > 0$.

conclusions: $H_p(\mathbf Z_{\mathcal U,\bullet})=0$ as an abelian presheaf for every $p>0$.

statement:
The assertions in this section concern **abelian presheaves**, not abelian sheaves; the functor and exactness claims must not be transferred to sheaf categories. Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ a family of maps with fixed target and all finite iterated fibre products over $U$, and consider abelian presheaves on $\mathcal C$. The complex $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal U,\bullet}$ is the alternating free-representable presheaf complex from sites-cohomology.tex:970–1003, and $\otimes_{p,\mathbf Z}$ is the tensor product of presheaves over the constant presheaf of integers.

\begin{slogan}
The integral presheaf {\v C}ech complex is a flat resolution of the
constant presheaf of integers.
\end{slogan}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let
$\mathcal{U} = \{f_i : U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms
with fixed target such that all fibre products
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p}$ exist in $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a presheaf of rings on $\mathcal{C}$.
The chain complex
$$
\mathbf{Z}_{\mathcal{U}, \bullet}
\otimes_{p, \mathbf{Z}}
\mathcal{O}
$$
is exact in positive degrees. Here $\mathbf{Z}_{\mathcal{U}, \bullet}$
is the chain complex of Lemma \ref{lemma-cech-map-into}, and
the tensor product is over the constant presheaf of rings
with value $\mathbf{Z}$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a category with a fixed-target family $\mathcal U$ admitting all iterated fibre products.
$\mathcal O$ is a presheaf of rings on $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: The complex of presheaves $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal U,\bullet}\otimes_{p,\mathbf Z}\mathcal O$ is exact in all positive degrees.

statement:
The assertions in this section concern **abelian presheaves**, not abelian sheaves; the functor and exactness claims must not be transferred to sheaf categories. Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ a family of maps with fixed target and all finite iterated fibre products over $U$, and consider abelian presheaves on $\mathcal C$. $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\prod_{(i_0,\dots,i_p)}\mathcal F(U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_U U_{i_p})$ with the alternating restriction differential, and $\check H^p$ denotes its cohomology. The functor $\check H^0(\mathcal U,-):\mathrm{PAb}(\mathcal C)\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is left exact, and $R\check H^0$ denotes its right derived functor on bounded-below derived categories.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let
$\mathcal{U} = \{f_i : U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms
with fixed target such that all fibre products
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p}$ exist in $\mathcal{C}$.
The {\v C}ech cohomology functors $\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, -)$
are canonically isomorphic as a $\delta$-functor to
the right derived functors of the functor
$$
\check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, -) :
\textit{PAb}(\mathcal{C})
\longrightarrow
\textit{Ab}.
$$
Moreover, there is a functorial quasi-isomorphism
$$
\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})
\longrightarrow
R\check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})
$$
where the right hand side indicates the derived functor
$$
R\check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, -) :
D^{+}(\textit{PAb}(\mathcal{C}))
\longrightarrow
D^{+}(\mathbf{Z})
$$
of the left exact functor $\check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, -)$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a category and $\mathcal U$ is a fixed-target family admitting all iterated fibre products.
$\mathcal F$ is an abelian presheaf on $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: The Čech cohomology functors $\check H^p(\mathcal U,-)$ are canonically the right derived functors $R^p\check H^0(\mathcal U,-)$, as cohomological $\delta$-functors.
There is a functorial quasi-isomorphism of complexes $\check{\mathcal C}^{\bullet}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to R\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$.

\label{lemma-cech-cohomology-derived-presheaves}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let
$\mathcal{U} = \{f_i : U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms
with fixed target such that all fibre products
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p}$ exist in $\mathcal{C}$.
The {\v C}ech cohomology functors $\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, -)$
are canonically isomorphic as a $\delta$-functor to
the right derived functors of the functor
$$
\check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, -) :
\textit{PAb}(\mathcal{C})
\longrightarrow
\textit{Ab}.
$$
Moreover, there is a functorial quasi-isomorphism
$$
\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})
\longrightarrow
R\check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})
$$
where the right hand side indicates the derived functor
$$
R\check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, -) :
D^{+}(\textit{PAb}(\mathcal{C}))
\longrightarrow

$$
of the left exact functor $\check{H}^0(\mathcal{U}, -)$.
